title: Interpretation at Risk: Post-Interpretive Criticism After the 20th Century
author: Dorian Vale

title: Moral Proximity: Ethics as Method in Post-Interpretive Criticism
author: Dorian Vale
summary: An essay developing moral proximity as a method of critical responsibility. It considers the relation between descriptive restraint, custodianship, and encounters with works concerned with trauma or absence.

title: The Afterlife of the Work: Viewer as Evidence in Post-Interpretive Criticism
author: Dorian Vale
summary: An essay treating the lasting effects of an encounter with art as evidence within Post-Interpretive Criticism. Its focus is the viewer’s memory, response, and continuing responsibility to the work.

title: Language as Custody — Writing Without Harm in Post-Interpretive Criticism
author: Dorian Vale
summary: An essay considering how language may protect or distort the ethical force of artworks. It develops restraint in writing as a form of custodianship, particularly around trauma, silence, and exile.
